correctness.rationale: For real n-site signals and odd cyclic windows m=2r+1<=n, all strict-order chambers have selector Jacobians J with one 1 in each row. Their exact ell_p operator norm is max_j c_j^(1/p), and continuity through order ties makes the largest chamber norm the global two-input Lipschitz constant. All m windows containing a chosen site select it iff each has exactly r below-signs. Consecutive-window comparison imposes chi_j=chi_(j+k) on sites 1..n-1 with k=n-m; the k residue chains contribute weights q or q+1 when 2r=qk+t. This establishes the iff subset-sum a(q+1)+bq=r, 0<=a<=t, 0<=b<=k-t, including n=m separately. n odd and n>=4r+1 admit explicit balancing; n=m+1 yields maximal column count r+1, and direct witness gives count 6 for (n,r)=(10,3). Infinity-norm 1 follows median monotonicity and constant translations. Independent bitmask enumeration for small r,n reproduced the multiplicities; finite tests do not prove the universal claim.
residual_risks: The theorem is about odd-window cyclic equal-coordinate ell_p norms. It does not classify all non-saturating norms, even windows, weights, or noncyclic boundary conditions.
